sentences.text: Borealonectes is a member of the Rhomaleosauridae family, a group of plesiosaurs that includes the pliosauroid subgroup.
The name translates to 'northern swimmer' in Greek.
It holds the distinction of being the first marine reptile from the Canadian Arctic with a well-preserved skull.
This species is one of the very few plesiosaurs known from the Jurassic period of North America.
Scientists Sato and Wu formally named the genus in 2008.
Remains were uncovered in the Hiccles Cove Formation on Melville Island, Canada.
The description relies on the skull, neck vertebrae, and right forelimb of a single individual.
This animal lived during the Callovian stage, between 165.3 and 161.5 million years ago.
